}}'''Snegulka Detoni''' ('''de Toni''') (22 May 1921 – 14 January 2016) was a prominent Slovene physicist and chemist known for her research in [[Hydrogen bond|hydrogen bonding]]. She was the recipient of the Boris Kidrič Prize in 1961.

Detoni was the first female researcher in the [[University of Ljubljana]]'s physics department.<ref>{{Citation|last=Hadži|first=Dušan|pages=213–266|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.|language=en|doi=10.1002/9780470771587.ch6|isbn=9780470771587|last2=Detoni|first2=Snegulka|title=Acid Derivatives: Vol. 1 (1979)|year=1979}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.notranjci.si/osebe/detoni-snegulka/582/|title=DETONI Snegulka|last=Qualitas|website=www.notranjci.si|access-date=2018-10-09}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Detoni was awarded the Boris Kidrič Prize in 1961 along with [[Robert Blinc]] for her work in hydrogen bonding research.
